title: Four days with Scobey's band at the Continental
summary: Hodes describes the Continental job, the band members, Dave Black and Clancy Hayes, and the singer Toni Scott.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: This was on -- not Bourbon Street, but the other one, runs alongside. The Continental was the first job.
Walton. Playboy magazine started somewhere in this street, because the guy came in and sat with us.
Yeah, he opened their first Playboy club there.

So that's the time, and I worked four days with the band, and made the record, 'Rampin' and Stompin'" Victor with them. I was very impressed with the band. Dave Black on drums, Rich Madison playing tuba, I think Beebee and that tall clarinet player on the West Coast, can't think of his name. He was with the band at that time. And, [Hicks] Huges of course, Clancy was playing banjo, and just had a -- they did an hour and 15 minute show that knocked me out.
And then they had this Toni Scott who later got famous and got out of reach for which I was very grateful.

Yeah, she became a purist -- modernist after she got discovered. This music was not her bag. She was now into 'Little Boy Blue' or something, I forgot. These tunes that the modernists -- if you sing them, you're hip. She got into that.
